plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of static gain and dominant lag/time constant, which determines steady-state power for 0.5 and safe controller aggressiveness.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises from ~0.12 with short lag toward 0.3-0.5 over 200 s with diminishing but still positive slope, confirming positive gain and giving first lag/gain estimate.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Decay to ambient and cooling time constant (H2/H3), which determines passive cool-down rate, ambient offset for feedforward, and safe integral time for control.
experiments.expected_observation: y decays from ~0.506 toward ~0.12-0.18 exponentially with time constant ~80-120 s, reaching <0.25 by end with slope near zero. If H2/H3 right, early drop ~0.05-0.10 in first 60-100 s then slowing.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Static gain at a second amplitude and steady-state u needed to hold 0.5, which sets controller feedforward and tests linearity.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises from ~0.15 after ~15-30 s lag toward ~0.40-0.50 over 300 s with diminishing but still positive slope, confirming gain ~1.0 and that u~0.3-0.4 holds near target.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain near target and exact feedforward for y=0.5, which sets controller bias and integral effort and distinguishes u_ss~0.35 vs 0.41.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises from ~0.446 toward ~0.48-0.51 over 160 s with diminishing positive slope (~0.0005-0.001/s at end), confirming K~0.8-0.9 and that u~0.40-0.42 holds y=0.5. If instead y stalls near 0.45, gain is lower and u_ss is higher.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain / feedforward for y=0.5 (H4): extending the current u=0.35 hold to near-settling distinguishes y_ss(0.35)~0.50-0.53 (K~1.0-1.1, u_ss~0.34) from lower-gain alternative y_ss~0.45, which sets controller bias and integral effort.
experiments.expected_observation: If K~1.05, y rises from ~0.474 toward ~0.49-0.52 over 150 s with diminishing positive slope approaching ~0 (mean ~0.49, slope |<0.0005|/s), entering/staying near band; if instead y stalls near 0.46, gain is lower and u_ss is higher.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Precise local gain and feedforward u_ss for y=0.5 (H4/H5): a small step down from 0.35 to 0.30 distinguishes u_ss~0.32 vs 0.35 and measures settling near target, which sets controller bias and integral effort for staying in +-0.025 band.
experiments.expected_observation: y declines from ~0.533 toward ~0.49-0.51 over 170s with initially negative slope flattening to near zero, confirming y_ss(0.30)~0.47-0.49 and that u_ss for 0.5 is ~0.31-0.33. If y instead stays ~0.53, gain is lower/nonlinear.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Precise feedforward u_ss for y=0.5 (H4/H5): a 0.30-to-0.32 near-target hold distinguishes u_ss~0.32 from 0.30 and measures settling slope, which sets controller bias and integral effort for staying in 0.475-0.525.
experiments.expected_observation: y starts ~0.50 and stays near band, drifting slightly toward ~0.49-0.51 with flattening slope (|slope|<0.001/s) and mean ~0.50, confirming y_ss(0.32)~0.50 and u_ss~0.32. If y instead rises to ~0.53 or falls to ~0.47, gain/feedforward estimate is off.

ledger.statement: Increasing heater power u increases steady-state temperature y (positive static gain).
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.14-0.16 over minutes due to heat loss.
Step response has ~20-30 s initial flat/lag then first-order lag with time constant ~150-200 s.
Steady-state is y_ss ~0.15 + K*u with K~1.0-1.1, so u~0.31-0.33 holds y=0.5; u=0.35 settles ~0.52-0.54.
Response has no large dead zone; gain is roughly linear from u=0.30 to 0.50.
Sensor has ~0.005-0.015 typical jitter plus occasional 0.02-0.08 downward outliers, so trends >0.05 over >30 s are real response.
